rate: 4% of financing value per year (flat, for the whole tenure) + savings of 5% of financing value per year
tenure: Up to 10 years (SPM and SPK up to 5 yrs; SPS up to 10 yrs)
age_rule: 18-65 at application; financing must end by 65
min_operating: not stated (application form covers both existing and new businesses)
other_criteria: Bumiputera Malaysian citizen; not bankrupt; companies 100% Bumiputera- and Malaysian-owned; valid PBT licence/permit or SSM registration; fixed, mobile or online business location; owner directly involved full- or part-time; one financing per household; paid-up capital ≤ RM300k; Shariah-compliant activity; group financing takaful mandatory; SKSPS self-employed social security mandatory for year 1. First financing: SPK RM10,001–50,000 or SPS RM50,001–100,000; SPM RM1,000–10,000 is for repeat/overlapping financing only
documents: Copy of IC of applicant and spouse if applicable (front and back); PBT licence/permit or SSM business registration; photos showing the business in operation; latest 3 months savings/current account bank statements showing applicant/company name, bank name and account number; additional documents if applicable
how_to_apply: TEKUN branch counter near the business, or TEKUN Online (tekunonline.tekun.gov.my); 03-9059 8888
notes: Old source URL (English conditions page) now returns 404. That page said age 18–60, ≥20% own cash for new businesses and other business financing ≤ RM100k; the current official page does not list those conditions. Rates are flat on original principal, so effective rate is higher (RinggitPlus, Jun 2026). One-time wakalah fee from RM50 to RM500 depending on amount.

other_criteria: For online businesses; cap RM5,000 without SSM registration
documents: Not listed
how_to_apply: Online via TEKUN

rate: not stated (AIM general: ~10% p.a. per RinggitPlus)

status: Closed (official application form); no 2026 round found on BSN or MDEC pages

agency: Bank Negara Malaysia via participating FIs; guarantee by CGC/SJPP
other_criteria: Viable but materially affected by trade/supply-chain disruption from the Middle East conflict (since Mar 2026); working capital only; no refinancing; up to 80% guarantee from CGC or SJPP, no collateral; RM750k cap across all banks; open to new and existing bank customers; RM10 billion facility
documents: Bank statements and transaction records; CCRIS account conduct data; audited financial statements or management accounts; sales records, invoices, purchase orders; supplier contracts/correspondence showing cost increases, delays or cancellations; stock movement records; debtor/creditor ageing reports; final list set by each bank
deadline: 15 May 2026 to 30 Jun 2027 or until fully utilised (BNM FAQ latest update 9 Oct 2026 and brochure; the 15 May 2026 FAQ said 31 Dec 2026)
how_to_apply: Any participating bank / Islamic bank / DFI; decision target 7 business days
source_type: Official (BNM SME SRF FAQ, latest update 9 Oct 2026; also https://www.bnm.gov.my/funds4sme and brochure https://www.bnm.gov.my/documents/20124/6025157/SME-SRF-Brochure-EN-8.pdf)
notes: Deadline conflict resolved: BNM's FAQ (latest update 9 Oct 2026), brochure and funds page all say 30 Jun 2027; the FAQ now gives a RM10 billion facility (the 15 May 2026 FAQ said RM5 billion). Working capital only, so it cannot fund renovation or equipment capex. Strong demo hook: supplier price-rise invoices ARE the 'impact evidence' BNM lists.

program: Micro Enterprises Facility (MEF) / Skim Pembiayaan Mikro
agency: Bank Negara Malaysia via participating FIs
rate: Varies by bank (BNM list as at 27 Jul 2026), e.g. BSN Mikro/i Madani 3.5%/4.0% flat; Bank Islam iTEKAD Maju 4% effective; Bank Rakyat MUsK MEF 6.5% flat
min_operating: 6 months to 3 years depending on product
other_criteria: Microenterprises, social enterprises, professional service providers, self-employed incl. gig workers; no collateral (third-party guarantee may be required)
documents: IC of applicant/owners; proof of business operations (registration/licence/permit); proof of income (usually latest 6 months bank statements, sales records, or Form B/BE with tax receipt); other documents per bank (e.g. Maybank: 2 years audited or management accounts; Bank Islam iTEKAD: application form and utility bill)
how_to_apply: Participating FIs (BNM list as at 27 Jul 2026): Agrobank, Alliance, AmBank, Bank Islam, Bank Muamalat, Bank Rakyat, BSN, CIMB Islamic, Maybank, Public Bank, RHB (+ UOB)
notes: Range of effective rates is wide (AmBank 13.5–18% effective). Agent should rank by effective rate. BSN Mikro/i Madani has a Madani Wanita variant for women entrepreneurs. Documents differ by bank; the bnm.gov.my/microfinance page lists each bank's own list.

rate: DanaNITA 3.5% profit rate; SEMAi 4%; basis (flat or reducing) not stated
ownership: Bumiputera Malaysian citizen; DanaNITA: majority 51% shareholding by women
other_criteria: DanaNITA (up to RM150k, Bumiputera women expanding a business): SSM registration; business premises (except online businesses); PBT licence/permit (waived for ≤ RM50k); full-time business; active savings account for latest 6 months; experience/knowledge in the business; Shariah-compliant; not on MARA blacklist; scope = working capital, machines and equipment; no guarantor/collateral for ≤ RM50k, above that a guarantor, land collateral or 10% fixed deposit; grace period up to 12 months. SEMAi (RM10k–50k, 4%) is only for MARA education institution (IPMa) graduates and covers premises renovation. PUTRA: youth ≤40, up to RM10k. SPiM: Bumiputera capacity/expansion up to RM500k. SPiKE: contractors, up to RM1m
documents: No full checklist published (applications via MyUsahawan login). Items named in DanaNITA conditions: SSM registration; PBT licence/permit (waived ≤ RM50k); bank statements for 3 months (online statements accepted); quotation for renovation or machinery (waived ≤ RM50k); guarantor, land collateral or fixed-deposit documents if > RM50k. Confirm full list with MARA
how_to_apply: Online via MyUsahawan (myusahawan.mara.gov.my) or MARA district office; MARA hotline 03-2613 2000
source_type: Official (mara.gov.my DanaNITA page; SEMAi page https://www.mara.gov.my/bm/menu_keusahawanan/kemudahan-sokongan/pembiayaan-perniagaan-2/semai/; scheme list https://www.mara.gov.my/bm/menu_keusahawanan/kemudahan-sokongan/pembiayaan-perniagaan-2/)
notes: Correction: the 2023 brochure mapping was wrong. On mara.gov.my, SEMAi is for IPMa graduates (max RM50k) and the Bumiputera-women scheme up to RM150k is DanaNITA. ID kept as MARA-SEMAI so existing links work. DanaNITA scope lists working capital and machines/equipment, not renovation. Pages carry no update date (site copyright 2025).

type: Membership initiative: micro financing + Cashline-i + Ar-Rahnu
rate: Micro financing via MRP 2.0 (the related product named in the T&C): from 4.75% p.a. on monthly rest; Cashline-i: BFR + 2.5% p.a.
tenure: MRP 2.0 up to 7 years (84 months); Cashline-i up to 5 years (annual review)
ownership: Individuals or non-individuals registered as SMEs and below; Malaysian citizen (MRP 2.0, Cashline-i)
age_rule: 21 at application to 70 at end of financing (MRP 2.0, Cashline-i)
other_criteria: Join by opening an Agro Tani Saudagar-i (individual) or Agro Perdana Saudagar-i (non-individual) account; existing Agrobank micro/hawker customers join automatically; Shariah-compliant business. MRP 2.0 (RM1k–100k): micro enterprise per SME Corp definition; no collateral; covers operating costs and purchase or development of fixed assets; refinancing allowed. Also Cashline-i RM1k–5k and Ar-Rahnu up to RM300k
sectors: Hawkers / micro F&B and other Shariah-compliant micro businesses (MRP 2.0 focuses on the food production value chain)
documents: Membership account (individual): MyKad; valid PBT business licence. Micro financing (MRP 2.0): completed application form; copy of IC (and joint applicant's, if any); latest 12 months savings account statements or sales records; copy of business registration or licence (fixed premises); any accepted proof of income
status: Open (product page live; T&C and FAQ dated May 2026; nationwide with GPPPKMM from Jul 2026)
how_to_apply: Any Agrobank branch (individual account can also be opened online); 1-300-88-2476
source_type: Official (Agrobank product page + programme T&C and FAQ PDFs, May 2026; MRP 2.0 page https://www.agrobank.com.my/product/microenterprise-special-relief/)
notes: Most F&B-specific scheme in the DB. Membership gives access to offers; each financing still needs its own approval. T&C section 2 names MRP 2.0 as the related micro-financing product. agrobank.com.my serves an incomplete TLS certificate chain, so some automated fetchers fail on it.
